Data and analytics · Structure · Tested
In 1 minute

Data pipeline failure triage

Emanuel · Data Operations Analyst

A retailer's data team runs 220 overnight load tasks and receives 15 to 40 failure alerts every night, 70% of them solved by a rerun or by waiting.

When it runs
With every failure alert the orchestrator posts in the data incidents channel on Slack, with a consolidation of the night's alerts at 6 a.m.
What it delivers in production
A reply to every alert in under 3 minutes with class, log evidence and proposed action for the on-call engineer to approve; a summary at 6 a.m.; and new runbooks opened by pull request for failures that repeat.
Who decides
Classifies and proposes; on-call approves
Effort
Calibrate 100 failures; 3 weeks in proposal mode
Set up5 steps · 9 ready files

# Load failure classification guide

## Classes
- Transient: timeout, read timed out, connection reset.
- Source unavailable: connection refused, host unreachable, source under maintenance.
- Schema change: column or table added, removed or renamed at the source.
- Invalid data: value out of format in a record.
- Code error: exception from the code itself (NameError, TypeError, SyntaxError).
- Delayed dependency: upstream task has not finished yet.

## Rules that settle doubts
- First real error line: the first ERROR line of the run. WARN and stack lines (starting with "at" or "File") do not count. The alert excerpt may be generic: the log prevails.
- Time failure = timeout or read timed out. 7-day window = the alert day and the 6 days before. The third time failure of the same task in that window becomes a recurring SOURCE UNAVAILABLE: tag the owner.
- Citable history = the alert day and the 29 days before.
- Log line with a CPF (individual tax ID), e-mail or customer name: cite only the line number, with the excerpt replaced by [personal data removed].

## Source, owner and report of each task
| Task | Source | Owner | Closing with report by 7 a.m. |
|---|---|---|---|
| pos_sales_daily_load | POS | Sales Eng. | no |
| store_stock_daily_load | WMS | Stock Eng. | yes, stock at 7 a.m. |
| erp_prices_load | ERP | Pricing Eng. | no |
| crm_customers_load | CRM | Customers Eng. | no |
| marketplace_orders_load | Marketplace B | Sales Eng. | no |
| finance_receivables_load | ERP | Finance Eng. | yes, financial position at 6:30 a.m. |

## Rules with no leeway
- Log line with a CPF, e-mail or customer name: in any block, including EVIDENCE and NIGHT SUMMARY, cite only the line number and the field name. No value from that line appears.
- Escalation tags add up: owner, on-call and tech lead receive every notice that applies to the task.
- A non-idempotent task never gets a simple rerun, not even when the runbook or the history says to rerun.

## Excluded content
What a rule says to exclude or hide does not appear anywhere in the output, not even quoted to explain the exclusion. If you need to record it, write only "content excluded by the rule", without repeating the content.

## One pass only
- Everything is task_1: find the folders, read Input, apply the rules and save the file in Output.
- Do not build a plan with separate steps (locate, read, classify, write, save). A 1-task plan.

# Existing runbooks (runbooks/ folder on GitHub)

## runbooks/stock_load.md
1. Timeout at the WMS: wait 15 min and rerun only after the cleanup procedure.
2. WMS under maintenance: wait for the end of the window.
3. Column added or removed at the source: do not rerun. The owner updates the mapping, clears the partition of the reference day and runs the new load. Tell the Stock team that the 7 a.m. report comes out with D-2 data.

## runbooks/pos_sales_load.md
1. Timeout at the POS replica: rerun once; if it repeats, call the owner.

## runbooks/erp_prices_load.md
1. ERP in a maintenance window: wait for the end of the window; the next scheduled attempt runs on its own.

## runbooks/marketplace_load.md
1. Read timed out at the marketplace API: rerun (idempotent task).

No runbook: crm_customers_load and finance_receivables_load.

Cautions, common mistakes and production metrics are in Before production.

Before production

Cautions

A task marked as non-idempotent never receives a simple rerun proposal, even with a transient class, because a rerun without cleaning the partition duplicates records and the error reaches the report before anyone notices. A rerun is triggered only after explicit on-call approval; the agent has no permission to trigger the orchestrator on its own. A runbook drafted by the agent goes in through a pull request reviewed by the task owner, and log excerpts with customers' personal data are not copied to Slack.

Common mistakes

  • Rerunning a source-unavailable failure within the known maintenance window; the task fails again.
  • Classifying every connection timeout failure as transient; three nights in a row is source degradation, not chance.
  • Ignoring the dependency between tasks and rerunning the child load before the parent finishes, producing a success on incomplete data.
  • Treating a schema change as a code error and calling the developer; the action is to update the mapping with the source owner.

Metrics

MetricRangeSource
Alerts requiring a manual on-call decisionfrom 100% to 30% to 40% after allowing reruns of transient failuresestimate based on the described routine
Time between the alert and the decided actionfrom 20 to 45 minutes to less than 5 minutesestimate based on the described routine
Undue reruns of non-idempotent taskszero, verified in calibration with 100 failures and monitored monthlyestimate based on the described routine

Sample production output

Fictional sample. Reply to the alert of 2026-09-01 03:12, task daily_store_stock_load.

CLASS: SCHEMA CHANGE (confidence 0.92)
EVIDENCE: log line 214: 'column qty_reserved not found in source'; the WMS source published a new version at 1:50 a.m. according to the history; last failure of this class on this task: 2026-06-04, solved by updating the mapping.
IDEMPOTENCY: task NOT idempotent (inserts without a key); a rerun without cleanup duplicates the day's stock.
PROPOSED ACTION: do not rerun. Open a task for the owner to adjust the column mapping and clean the 2026-08-31 partition before the new load. Warn the stock team that the 7 a.m. report will go out with yesterday's data.
EXISTING RUNBOOK: yes, runbooks/stock_load.md section 3, applicable.
AWAITING: on-call approval.

(6 a.m.) NIGHT SUMMARY: 23 alerts | transient 14 (13 rerun with approval, 1 failed again and became a late dependency) | source unavailable 5 (waiting for the ERP window at 6:30 a.m.) | schema change 2 | code error 1 | invalid data 1. Average time to decision: 4 min. On-call corrections to the proposals: 1 in 23.

alert.json with task, time, error_excerpt. Full run_log.txt. failure_history.csv with task, date, class, action, result. runbooks/*.md. idempotency.csv with task, idempotent (yes or no), cleanup_procedure. windows.csv with system, maintenance_start, end, contact.

RESPONSIBILITIES
1. Find in the log the first real error line, ignoring warnings and the repeated stack.
2. Classify as transient, source unavailable, schema change, invalid data, code error or delayed dependency; assign a confidence from 0 to 1.
3. Check the same task's history: if the same class occurred in the last 30 days, cite the date and the action that worked.
4. Check idempotency; if not idempotent, a rerun is only admissible with the cleanup procedure.
5. Check whether the source is in a maintenance window; if so, the action is to wait until the end of the window, and cite the time.
6. Find the applicable runbook section or state that none exists.
7. Propose a single, objective action and say who to notify about the report delay.

RULES AND LIMITS
Never propose a simple rerun for a non-idempotent task. Do not copy into the answer log lines with a CPF, e-mail or customer name. Do not classify as transient the third time failure of the same task in 7 days. Confidence below 0.6 requires writing UNCERTAIN CLASS and listing both hypotheses.

OUTPUT FORMAT
Blocks CLASS (with confidence), EVIDENCE (log line and history), IDEMPOTENCY, PROPOSED ACTION, EXISTING RUNBOOK, WAITING. In the 6 a.m. consolidation, NIGHT SUMMARY with count by class, approved actions, average time and on-call corrections.

ESCALATION
Transient in an idempotent task: rerun proposed for one-click approval. Source unavailable outside a known window for more than 60 minutes, or code error: tag the task owner besides on-call. Failure in a task that feeds the stock or finance closing with a report by 7 a.m.: tag the tech lead immediately, whatever the class.
